title: Put your Craft Block build into Minecraft — step by step
meta_desc: How to get a build from Craft Block into Minecraft: a ready world with your builds already in it (Bedrock), or your own world on Bedrock (phone, tablet, console, Windows) and Java (PC, Mac). One action per step, no mods.
og_title: Put your Craft Block build into Minecraft
og_desc: Bedrock and Java, no mods: a ready world with your builds already in it, or your own world with one command.

lead_028: Craft Block turns the build on your screen into a file the game understands. You open that file in Minecraft, type one command, and the same build appears in your world, block for block, at real size.
lead_029: Every step is one screen. The line under each says what you should see when it worked. The pictures are from an Android tablet and an iPhone; Windows looks the same.
lead_030: Java reads the build from a small .zip file you drop into your world's folder. Nothing to install.

see_032: You should see: the world settings, with a list of sections on the left (General, Game, Resource Packs, Behavior Packs…).

oops_042: Nothing happened, or the file opened somewhere else? Send the file to yourself (Telegram, Drive, mail), open it on the device, press and hold it → Open with → Minecraft.
oops_043: No Activate button? You are inside a running world — that screen only shows packs. Leave the world (pause → Save & Quit) and come back through the pencil, as in step 2.
oops_044: “Incorrect permission level for command: function” Cheats are on but your player is not an operator yet. Pause → Social (top right) → tap your own name → Operator. Type the command again.
oops_045: “Unknown command: craft_my_house” The word function went missing — easy to lose on a touch keyboard. Two words: /function craft_my_house.
oops_046: “Cheats aren't enabled in this world” Step 3 is not done: pause → Settings → Cheats in the left list → switch on. Creative alone does not turn cheats on.
oops_047: Your text shows up as a chat message The slash at the start went missing. Commands begin with / — on the iPhone keyboard it is under 123.
oops_048: “Unknown function” Step 4 is not done for this world, or you are in a different world. Spaces in the build's name become underscores: My House → craft_my_house.
oops_049: Says the pack is “incompatible”? Enable it anyway, it loads. Exports from Craft Block 2.6.0 and later do not show this.
oops_050: Commands do not work? Cheats are off for this world. Pause → Open to LAN → Allow Cheats: ON → Start LAN World. Creative worlds have cheats on already.
oops_051: “Unknown function” Step 4 was skipped, or the name is off: Java uses a colon and spaces become underscores — My House → craft:my_house.

p_071: A few steps, one thing to do in each. With a ready world your builds are already standing there when you open it. Or one command puts a build into a world you already have. No mods.
p_072: Home screen → press and hold a build → Export to Minecraft. Any build works: your own, or one of the examples.
p_073: Bedrock if you installed Minecraft from the App Store, Google Play, the Microsoft Store, or play on Xbox, PlayStation or Switch. Java if you start it from the Minecraft Launcher on a PC or Mac. Not sure? On the game's title screen Bedrock shows a version like v1.21.x in the corner; Java shows Minecraft 1.21.x and the Launcher.
p_074: Bedrock: either a ready world, one file ending in .mcworld that opens as a new world, or a pack, one file ending in .mcpack that adds a pack named after your build to the game. Java: one .zip ending in _datapack.zip that goes into your world's folder. All of them are tiny and hold only your builds, nothing else.
p_075: The app shows the size before you export: how many blocks, how wide, deep and tall. Bigger builds are cut into several parts inside the same file; the command still places all of them at once.
p_076: Carries over: every block, including stairs, slabs, doors, torches, glass, water, plants, with the direction you gave them.
p_077: Replaced: a few blocks exist only in Craft Block. The app lists each one and what the game gets instead (for example a lotus becomes a pink tulip). Nothing is dropped silently.
p_078: Stays in the app: animals and other creatures (they are decorations, the game has no block for them), and any texture pack you imported — the game uses its own textures.
p_079: Wherever you stand when you type the command. The build starts at your feet and grows east and south, so face east first. Details and a way to preview the exact spot are further down, in Where exactly does it appear?
p_080: Three builds are free in total. Every build that goes into the game uses one free export, so a ready world with three builds in it uses all three. After that, export is part of Craft Block Premium. The file itself never expires: once you have it, you can put the build into as many worlds as you like.
p_081: On the home screen press and hold your build → Export to Minecraft → Into your own world (under Bedrock) → Save .mcpack.
p_082: Then get the file into the game — this is the one step that differs by device:
p_083: Android phone or tablet: Minecraft opens by itself and imports the pack.
p_084: iPhone or iPad: a share sheet opens. Pick Minecraft. If it is not in the list, choose Save to Files, then open the Files app and tap the file.
p_085: Windows 10/11 (Bedrock from the Microsoft Store): send the file to the PC (mail, OneDrive, a cable) and double-click it. Minecraft starts and imports it.
p_086: Xbox, PlayStation, Switch: a console cannot open files. Import the pack on a phone or PC, put the build into a world there, and bring that world to the console through a Realm (Play on Realms → upload the world; the console then joins it). Or simply play that world on the phone.
p_087: In Minecraft press Play. You are on the Worlds tab.
p_088: New world: Create New → Create New World. Existing world: tap the pencil next to its name — not the name itself.
p_089: Left list → Cheats → switch Cheats on (on older versions it sits under Game as Activate Cheats). The game warns that achievements will be off in this world — that is fine, say yes. While you are here, General → Game Mode → Creative makes building easier.
p_090: Left list → Behavior Packs → open My Packs → tap the pack with your build's name → Activate.
p_091: If the game asks Update world?, choose Add the pack anyway — it only warns that the world will contain something it did not make.
p_092: Press Create (new world) or Play (existing). Walk to flat, open ground. Turn so the sun is in front of you when it rises — that is east. The build will fill the ground in front of you and to your right.
p_093: Tap the speech bubble at the top of the screen to open chat. The app put the command on your clipboard when you saved the file: hold the chat field → Paste. Or type it — it is two words with a space, the word function, then your build's name. For a build called My House:
p_094: Press send. The build appears at once.
p_095: On the home screen press and hold your build → Export to Minecraft → Java → Save .zip. Send the file to your computer any way you like: AirDrop, mail, Telegram, a cable. Do not unzip it.
p_096:
Mac: in Finder press ⌘⇧G, paste ~/Library/Application Support/minecraft/saves, Enter.
Windows: press WinR, type %appdata%\.minecraft\saves, Enter.
Linux: open ~/.minecraft/saves.
p_097: Open the folder with your world's name, then the datapacks folder inside it.
p_098: Move the file into datapacks. Still zipped.
p_099: Open the world in the game. Press T for chat and type these two lines, one after the other. Use your file's name in the first one:
p_100: Walk to flat, open ground. Press F3 (Mac: fnF3) and turn until the line Facing says east. The build will fill the ground in front of you and to your right.
p_101: Press T and type the command from the app (on the phone, the Copy button next to it puts it on the clipboard). In Java it has a colon. For a build called My House:
p_102: Face east (the sun rises there) and the build fills the ground in front of you and to your right. The app tells you how wide, deep and tall it is. The build is placed as-is: over a hill, part of it ends up inside the hill; over a lake, the water gets in. Flat ground first, command second.
p_103: The game's own structure block draws the build's outline before placing it, and lets you nudge and rotate it. Get one with /give @s structure_block, place it, open it, set the mode to Load, type your build's name in the name field (craft:my_house in both editions), turn on the bounding box, adjust the offsets until the outline sits right, then Load. One block holds up to 48 blocks per side in Java and 64 in Bedrock; bigger builds come as several parts and the app lists the offset of each.
p_104: They need solid ground under them. If the build landed over a dip, a hole or water, the game drops them the moment they load. Place it on flat ground, or fill the ground first.
p_105: Your build has a pond or a pool and was placed above the ground, so the water had nowhere to sit. Place it lower, on the ground, and the water stays in its basin.
p_106: The game decides a stair's corner shape from its neighbours, exactly as when you place one by hand. A corner stair with no stairs next to it is straight; in a finished roof it is a corner.
p_107: Animals in Craft Block are decorations, not blocks. The game has no block for them, so they stay in the planner. The app tells you how many before you export.
p_108: Consoles cannot open files, so the pack cannot be imported there directly. Import it on a phone, tablet or PC (step 1 above), place the build in a world, then upload that world to a Realm and join the Realm from the console. Without a Realm, the build stays on the device you imported it on.
p_109: No. Any game mode works, Survival included — the only thing the command needs is cheats switched on for that world, and cheats only cost you the achievements there. Creative is just easier for looking the build over: you can fly, and nothing bites.
p_110: Three builds are free in total; a ready world uses one free export for each build in it. After that, export is part of Craft Block Premium. Everything on this page is done by the game itself and costs nothing.

h2_113: Bedrock, the easiest way: Ready world
lead_114: Craft Block makes a brand-new flat Creative world with your build already standing in it. No commands to type, nothing to switch on, and your own worlds stay untouched. Want the build inside a world you already have? Use Into your own world below.
p_116: On the home screen press and hold your build → Export to Minecraft → Ready world, the first choice under Bedrock.
p_118: The app asks Which builds go into the world? The one you are exporting is already ticked. Add more from Your builds and Built-in examples, up to 10 in all, then press Create world.
p_119: They will stand side by side on a flat plain, in rows. Premium examples appear in the list with Craft Block Premium. Without Premium, each build uses one of your free exports, so the list lets you add as many as you have left.
h3_120: Get the world into the game
p_121: Press Save .mcworld. What happens next depends on the device:
p_122: Android phone or tablet: Minecraft opens by itself and imports the world. The game restarts to do it — that is normal.
p_124: Tap the new world. It has your build's name, with +2 on the end if you added two more. For a few seconds the line above the hotbar says Building your world… while the area loads.
see_125: You should see: your builds right in front of you (with many of them, you start on a small raised deck). It is Creative: fly around and walk inside.
oops_126: Achievements are off in this world. Cheats are on there, and Minecraft gives no achievements in a world with cheats. That is the trade, and it is why your own survival worlds are never touched. Into your own world below needs cheats in your own world instead, which turns its achievements off for good.
lead_127: Into your own world: the build goes into a world you already have. A few more steps: cheats on in that world, then one command.
